findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a client declares `packageManager: "pnpm@10.20.0"` before its first install, or keeps its pnpm app and lockfile under `web/`.
Not done: After forge sync, a pnpm client's generated workflow sets up pnpm before its tests run, so the tests check no longer fails with pnpm not found.
The new condition only checks for `pnpm-lock.yaml` at the repository root, so neither client gets a pnpm setup step and its tests still fail with pnpm missing. A root lockfile is also missed when there is no root `package.json` and the configured test command is a wrapper such as `./scripts/test.sh`: the enclosing Node detection at `src/forge/prcheck.py:237` never reaches this condition.
findings.title: Not done: Detect pnpm clients without a root pnpm-lock.yaml

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a pnpm client selects `windows-latest` through `test_runner` or `runner`.
GitHub-hosted Windows images already have a Yarn shim in npm's global prefix. Installing Corepack globally attempts to install another shim there and fails with `EEXIST` before `corepack enable` or the tests run. The scheduled full-suite job receives the same command when its runner is Windows. [Microsoft's workflow](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/blob/main/.github/workflows/extension-e2e-tests.yml) documents this conflict, and [npm's shim installer](https://github.com/npm/bin-links/blob/main/lib/shim-bin.js) rejects an existing shim owned by another package.
findings.title: Avoid the Corepack installation conflict on Windows runners

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an existing client has a pnpm lockfile and `engines.pnpm: "^10.33.0"`, but no `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager` field.
The generated command enables Corepack without selecting the client's pnpm version. On a fresh runner, [Corepack resolves its default from the registry](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/v0.36.0/sources/Engine.ts); the current pnpm 12 then [rejects an incompatible `engines.pnpm`](https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/12.19.0). The install and tests therefore fail even though the client's pnpm 10 lockfile is valid. The same setup is copied into the full-suite job.
findings.title: Respect the pnpm version of lockfile-only clients

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a pnpm client runs its generated workflow on Node 26.
The pnpm test calls `forge init` through `_fresh_client` (`tests/test_setup.py:218`), rather than `forge sync`, and only searches the output for the text `corepack enable`. It would pass for `run: corepack enable` alone, although [Node 26 does not bundle Corepack](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/deps/corepack/README.md) and that command would fail. It would also reject a working pnpm setup using an action. The npm negative test checks only for the word `corepack`, so an unwanted pnpm action would pass it. The required workflow behavior needs proof at the sync boundary.
findings.title: Gate: pnpm availability after sync

findings.body:
Gain 1, Work 1, Harm 1
The npm negative test copies a v1.2.2 adopted-client fixture and changes its version pin even though npm detection is an ordinary rule, not older-release behavior. The repository's review rules require ordinary rules to use a new repo and identify new earlier-adopted cases as deletion candidates. Keep the npm negative case on a fresh client instead.

why: After the upgrade from v1.2.28 to v1.2.40, the generated .github/workflows/forge.yml has no pnpm setup, so a pnpm workspace repo's tests check fails with pnpm not found (exit 127).
